articles.title: राँगाको सिङबाट बन्ने गुँला पर्वको मुख्य बाजा !
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेवार समुदायका विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीको प्रमुख सांस्कृतिक पर्व गुँला बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । एक महिनासम्म मनाइने पर्वमा भक्तजनले परम्परागत बाजागाजासहित चैत्य, विहार र मन्दिरको परिक्रमा गर्दै बुद्धको पूजा–आराधना गर्ने गर्दछन् ।

काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका परम्परागत नेवार वस्ती र टोलहरुमा अब एक महिनासम्म सडक वा गल्लीहरुमा विहान मानिसहरुको चहलपहल शुरु नहुँदै सुनिने छ, धिमे, भुस्या, बाँसुरी र न्याकुँको सुमधुर आवाज । अनि बाजाको यही धुन पछ्याउँदै मानिसहरू चैत्यतर्फ अघि बढिरहेका हुने छन् । यो गुँला पर्वको अवसरमा देखिने दृश्य हो ।

नेवार समुदायमा पनि विशेषगरी बौद्ध धर्मावलम्बीले मनाउने गुँला पर्व बिहीबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ । श्रावण शुक्ल प्रतिपदादेखि भाद्र शुक्ल प्रतिपदासम्म चल्ने यो पर्व करिब एक महिनासम्म धार्मिक र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकालाई जीवन्त बनाउँछ ।

गुँला शब्दको अर्थ आफैमा रोचक पनि छ । नेपाल भाषामा ‘गुँ’ को अर्थ नौ र ‘ला’ को अर्थ महिना भन्ने गरिन्छ । नेपाल संवतको नवौँ महिनामा मनाइने भएकाले यसको नाम गुँला रहन गएको मानिन्छ । गुँलाको वास्तविक आकर्षण बिहानै सुरु हुने यात्रामा देखिन्छ । भक्तजनहरू परम्परागत बाजा बजाउँदै विभिन्न चैत्य, विहार, बहाः र बहीको परिक्रमा गर्छन् ।

काठमाडौंको स्वयम्भू, बौद्ध, पाटनलगायतका धार्मिक तथा ऐतिहासिक स्थलमा गुँला पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखिन्छ । एउटा समूह धिमे बजाउँदै अघि बढिरहेको हुन्छ । यसमा कसैले भुस्या बजाइरहेको हुन्छ भने कसैले न्याकुँको गहिरो आवाज निकालिरहेको हुन्छ । यही दृश्यले गुँलालाई काठमाडौँका अन्य धेरै जात्रा र पर्वहरुभन्दा फरक बनाएको छ ।

गुँला पूजा र परिक्रमा गर्ने पर्व मात्रै होइन । संगीत जोडिएको उपत्यकाको जीवित संस्कृति पनि हो । विशेषगरी न्याकुँ बाजा गुँलाको पहिचानसँग जोडिएको छ । राँगाको सिङबाट बनाइने यो बाजा हेर्दा साधारण देखिए पनि यसको ध्वनि निकै विशिष्ट हुन्छ ।

परम्परागत रूपमा धार्मिक यात्राहरुमा यसको प्रयोग हुँदै आएको छ । त्यसैगरी धिमे, बाँसुरी, भुस्या र धाः लगायतका बाजासँगै बज्दा यी आवाजले पनि गुँला पर्वमा सांगीतिक समूहको स्वरूप लिन्छन् । पछिल्लो समय यस्ता जात्रा पर्वमा नयाँ पुस्ताको सहभागिता पनि बढिरहेको छ । नयाँ पूस्ताको सहभागितासँगै परम्परागत पर्व र संस्कृति पुस्तान्तरण पनि हुँदैछन् ।

गुँला धार्मिक पर्व मात्रैमा सीमित छैन । सामाजिकरुपमा खेतीपातीको मुख्य काम सकिएको समयसँग पनि यो पर्व जोडिएको छ । मानिसहरू केही फुर्सदिला हुने यही समयमा समुदाय भेला हुने, भेटघाट गर्ने र सामूहिक रूपमा धार्मिक गतिविधिमा सहभागी हुने अवसर पनि गुँलाले जुटाइ दिएको छ ।

बौद्ध परम्परामा वर्षायामको साधना र धार्मिक अभ्याससँग पनि गुँला समयको सम्बन्ध जोडिन्छ । त्यसैले यो अवधि पूजा, ध्यान, पाठ, दान र पुण्यकर्मका लागि विशेष मानिन्छ । यसको अर्को पक्ष के भने गुँला पर्वमा हुने चैत्य परिक्रमा एउटा यात्रा मात्रै होइन ।

उपत्यकाका विभिन्न स्थानीय धार्मिक स्थललाई जोड्ने सांस्कृतिक नेटवर्क जस्तो पनि हो । एउटा टोलबाट अर्को टोल, एउटा बहाःबाट अर्को चैत्यसम्म बाजाको धुनले यी ठाउँहरूलाई जोडिरहेको हुन्छ । काठमाडौंलाई मन्दिरै–मन्दिरको सहर भनिन्छ । तर गुँला पर्वले कामठाडौँ बाजा, बहाः, बही र चैत्यहरूको पनि सहर हो भन्ने प्रमाण पनि दिन्छ । एक महिनासम्म बज्ने यी बाजाहरु पुर्खाको स्मृति हुन्, धार्मिक आस्था हुन् र पहिचानको आवाज हुन् ।

articles.title: काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णयकाे एनआरएनएद्वारा स्वागत
articles.summary:
काठमाडाैँ । काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगल कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेपछि गैरआवासीय नेपाली संघ (एनआरएनए) पोर्चुगलले उक्त निर्णयको स्वागत गर्दै नेपाल तथा पोर्चुगल सरकारप्रति आभार व्यक्त गरेको छ।

नेपाल सरकारको २०८३ साउन २६ गते बसेको मन्त्रिपरिषद् बैठकले पोर्चुगल सरकारलाई काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय खोल्न सहमति दिने निर्णय गरेको थियो। निकट भविष्यमा नै कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आउने अपेक्षा गरिएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलका अध्यक्ष सुजन लामा मोक्तानले जारी गरेको विज्ञप्तिमा काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीलाई विभिन्न कन्सुलर सेवा लिन सहज हुने उल्लेख गरिएको छ। विशेषगरी पारिवारिक पुनर्मिलन, भिसा तथा अन्य कन्सुलर सेवाका लागि हाल भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने बाध्यता कम हुने संघको विश्वास छ।

नयाँ सरकार गठन भएपछि काठमाडौंमा पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनाका लागि नेपाल सरकारको तर्फबाट आवश्यक पहल अघि बढाइएको थियो। सोही क्रममा परराष्ट्रमन्त्री शिशिर खनालले पोर्चुगलका राज्य तथा विदेश मामिलामन्त्री पाउलो राङ्गेलसँग टेलिफोन संवाद गरी कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापनालगायतका विषयमा कुराकानी गरेका थिए।

नेपाल सरकारको अनुरोध तथा त्यसपछिका कूटनीतिक पहलपछि पोर्चुगल सरकारले काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय स्थापना गर्ने निर्णय गरेको हो। एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले यसलाई पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपाली समुदायका लागि महत्वपूर्ण उपलब्धिका रूपमा लिएको छ।

नेपाल र पोर्चुगलबीच १ सेप्टेम्बर १९७६ मा औपचारिक कूटनीतिक सम्बन्ध स्थापना भएको थियो। लामो समयसम्म नेपालले पोर्चुगलमा आवासीय दूतावास स्थापना नगरेका कारण पोर्चुगलसम्बन्धी नेपाली कूटनीतिक जिम्मेवारी पेरिसस्थित नेपाली दूतावासले सम्हाल्दै आएको थियो।

नेपाल सरकारले सन् २०२५ मार्चमा लिस्बनमा आवासीय नेपाली राजदूतावास स्थापना गरेको थियो। लिस्बनमा स्थापना भएको नेपाली दूतावासका पहिलो आवासीय राजदूत प्रकाशमणि पौडेल हुन्।

दूतावासको औपचारिक उद्घाटन भने २० फेब्रुअरी २०२६ मा परराष्ट्र सचिव अमृतबहादुर रायको पोर्चुगल भ्रमणका क्रममा गरिएको थियो। यससँगै नेपाल–पोर्चुगल सम्बन्ध थप संस्थागत र प्रत्यक्ष बनेको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलको भनाइ छ।

पोर्चुगलमा नेपालीको यकिन तथ्यांक नभए पनि ६० हजारभन्दा बढी नेपाली रहेको अनुमान नेपाली दूतावासले गरेको छ। ठूलो संख्यामा नेपाली समुदाय रहेको पोर्चुगलका लागि काठमाडौंमै पोर्चुगलको कन्सुलर सेवा सुरु हुनु महत्वपूर्ण कदम भएको एनआरएनए पोर्चुगलले जनाएको छ।

काठमाडौंमा कन्सुलर कार्यालय सञ्चालनमा आएपछि पोर्चुगलमा रहेका नेपालीले सेवा लिन भारतको नयाँ दिल्लीसम्म पुग्नुपर्ने अवस्थाको अन्त्य हुने तथा समय र आर्थिक खर्चसमेत बचत हुने अपेक्षा गरिएको छ।

articles.title: अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अन्तर्राष्ट्रिय युवा दिवसको अवसरमा रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थको संयुक्त आयोजनामा गरिएको तारकेश्वर–६ स्थित महांकाल मन्दिर क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ कार्यक्रम सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

बुधबार बिहान ७ः३० बजेदेखि सञ्चालन गरिएको कार्यक्रममा ३५ जना रोटेरियन तथा रोट्रयाक्ट सदस्यहरूको सहभागिता रहेको थियो। सहभागीहरूले मन्दिर परिसर तथा आसपासका क्षेत्रमा सरसफाइ गर्दै फोहोर व्यवस्थापन र स्वच्छ वातावरण निर्माणसम्बन्धी जनचेतना फैलाएका छन् ।

कार्यक्रमले सार्वजनिक स्थलको स्वच्छता कायम राख्नुका साथै युवाहरूलाई सामाजिक सेवामा सक्रिय रूपमा सहभागी गराउने उद्देश्य राखेको आयोजकले जनाएको छ ।

रोटरीको Create Lasting Impact भन्ने मूल भावनाअनुसार आयोजित कार्यक्रममा सहभागीहरूले समुदायको विकास र वातावरण संरक्षणका लागि यस्ता सामाजिक अभियानलाई निरन्तरता दिनुपर्नेमा जोड दिएका छन् ।

रोटरी क्लब अफ गोंगबु र रोट्रयाक्ट क्लब अफ गोंगबु नर्थले आगामी दिनमा पनि समुदाय केन्द्रित विभिन्न सामाजिक तथा वातावरणीय कार्यक्रम सञ्चालन गर्ने जनाएको छ ।

articles.title: आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सद्वारा कर्णालीकी छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले कर्णाली प्रदेशबाट काठमाडौं आई जोरपाटीस्थित चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालय कक्षा १२ मा अध्ययनरत छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई शैक्षिक छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको छ । शिक्षाको माध्यमबाट विद्यार्थीको क्षमता विकास तथा उज्ज्वल भविष्य निर्माणमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा शीता शाहीलाई छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गरेको हो । आफ्नो जन्मस्थान कर्णाली प्रदेश भए पनि काठमाडौंमा रही अध्ययन गर्दै आएकी शीता शाहीलाई प्रदान गरिएको यस सहयोगले उनको शैक्षिक यात्रालाई थप सहज बनाउँदै उच्च शिक्षा तथा आगामी लक्ष्यतर्फ अघि बढ्न प्रेरणा प्रदान गर्ने विश्वास फाइनान्सले लिएको छ ।

छात्रवृत्ति प्रदान गर्दै आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सले छात्रा सीता शाहीलाई उज्ज्वल भविष्यका लागि हार्दिक बधाई तथा शुभकामना व्यक्त गरेको छ । साथै, आगामी दिनमा पनि अध्ययनमा निरन्तर मेहनत, लगनशीलता र समर्पणका साथ अघि बढ्दै उत्कृष्ट सफलता हासिल गर्न प्रोत्साहित गरेको छ ।

उक्त छात्रवृत्ति वितरण कार्यक्रमा आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्सका प्रबन्धक अच्युत पण्डित, बौद्ध शाखा प्रबन्धक अजय राज रेग्मी, बजार व्यवस्थापन प्रमुख सञ्जोक गुरुङ तथा बजार व्यवस्थापन अधिकृत सरिना श्रेष्ठ लगायत चामुण्डा माध्यमिक विद्यालयका प्रधानाध्यापक तथा शिक्षकहरू र सामाजिक अभियान्ता टेक राज शाहीको उपस्थितिमा सम्पन्न भएको थियो।

आइ.सि.एफ.सि. फाइनान्स लिमिटेडले आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्व (CSR) अन्तर्गत शिक्षा क्षेत्रलाई प्राथमिकतामा राख्दै आर्थिक तथा सामाजिक रूपमा सहयोगको आवश्यकता भएका विद्यार्थीको शैक्षिक विकासमा योगदान पु¥याउँदै आएको छ। कम्पनीले आगामी दिनमा पनि शिक्षा, स्वास्थ्य तथा अन्य सामाजिक क्षेत्रमा आफ्नो सामाजिक उत्तरदायित्वलाई निरन्तरता दिने प्रतिबद्धता व्यक्त गरेको छ ।

articles.title: भृकुटीमण्डपमा नयाँ गाडी र बाइकको मेला, इभीमा सबैको आकर्षण
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डपमा मंगलबारदेखि नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ सुरु भएको छ । ५५ वटा ब्रान्ड सहभागी यो एक्स्पोमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन प्रदर्शन गरिएका छन् ।

अटोप्रेमीहरूका लागि नयाँ गाडी खरिद गर्ने र नयाँ अपडेट बुझ्ने अवसर एक्स्पोले जुराएको छ । काठमाडौंको भृकुटीमण्डप अहिले नयाँ मोडलका गाडी, मोटरसाइकल र अत्याधुनिक मोबिलिटी प्रविधिले भरिएको छ । र, यो माहोलको अवसर नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो २०२६ ले जुटाएको हो । नेपाल अटोमोबाइल इम्पोर्टर्स एण्ड म्यानुफ्याक्चरर्स एशोसिएसन अर्थात् नाइमाले दोस्रोपटक आयोजना गरेको एक्स्पो मंगलबारदेखि सुरु भएको छ ।

नेपाल प्रहरीका महानिरीक्षक दानबहादुर कार्की र नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतुसिंह वैद्यले पानसमा बत्ती बालेर एक्स्पोको औपचारिक शुभारम्भ गरे । यसपटकको एक्स्पोमा ५५ वटा ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् । जसमा ४० भन्दा बढी नयाँ मोडलका सवारीसाधन सार्वजनिक तथा प्रदर्शन गरिँदैछन् ।

नयाँ गाडी वा बाइक किन्ने सोचमा रहेकाहरुलाई भृकुटीमण्डपमा जारी एक्स्पो उत्कृष्ट गन्तव्य हुन सक्छ । एक्स्पोमा चारपांग्रेतर्फ हुन्डाई, टाटा, टोयोटा, महिन्द्रा, किया, निसान, बीवाईडी, एमजी, सिट्रोन, ओमोडा एन्ड जेको, डेन्जा, जिकर, लीपमोटर, वुलिङ, ग्रेट वाल मोटर्सलगायतका ब्राण्ड सहभागी छन् ।

त्यसैगरी दुईपांग्रेतर्फ बजाज, होन्डा, टीभीएस, रोयल इन्फिल्ड, केटीएम, सुजुकी, एथर, याडिया, अल्ट्राभायोलेट, सीएफ मोटो, ट्रायम्फलगायतका ब्राण्डले आफ्ना नयाँ उत्पादन प्रदर्शनीमा राखेका छन् ।

कमर्सियल भेहिकलतर्फ पनि चेरी वान्डा, केरी, डोङफेङ, स्काइवर्थलगायतका ब्राण्डका गाडीहरु एक्स्पोमा देख्न सकिन्छ । एक्स्पोको अर्को आकर्षणमा रुपमा यहाँ रहेका स्टलहरु र छुट अफर रहेको छ । ग्राहकलाई आकर्षित गर्न कम्पनीहरूले आकर्षक तथा फरक शैलीका स्टल निर्माण गरेका छन् । विभिन्न ब्राण्डले विशेष छुट र अफरसमेत सार्वजनिक गरिरहेका छन् ।

नाइमाकी अध्यक्ष ऋतु सिंह वैद्यका अनुसार नेपालको अटोमोबाइल क्षेत्र विस्तारै विद्युतीय सवारीतर्फ अघि बढिरहेको छ । विद्युतीय सवारीले हरित अर्थतन्त्र निर्माणमा योगदान पु¥याइरहेको उनको भनाइ छ । उनले नेपालमा अटो कम्पोनेन्ट उद्योगलाई प्रोत्साहन गर्न सके एसेम्बल प्लान्टको सम्भावना अझ बलियो हुने बताएकी छन् ।

एक्स्पोमा सवारीसाधनसँगै बैंक तथा वित्तीय संस्था र बीमा कम्पनीको सहभागिता छ भने विभिन्न नलेज सिरिज पनि सञ्चालन भइरहेका छन् । नाइमा नेपाल मोबिलिटी एक्स्पो साउन ३१ गतेसम्म सञ्चालन हुनेछ ।

articles.title: घण्टाकर्णका आतंक र अन्त्यको कथा गथाँमुगः पर्व
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायले मंगलवार घण्टाकर्ण अर्थात् गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाएका छन् । घण्टाकर्ण दानवको अन्त्य गरिएको स्मरणमा मनाइने यो पर्वमा तीनखुट्टे राक्षसको आकृति बनाएर साँझ आगोमा जलाउँदै भूतप्रेत, रोगव्याधि र नकारात्मक शक्ति भगाउने परम्परा छ । गथाँमुगःको अवसरमा काठमाडौं, भक्तपुर र ललितपुरमा यो पर्वको विशेष रौनक देखियो ।

प्रत्येक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौंका गल्ली, चोक र दोबाटोमा नरकट, छ्वाली र काठबाट एउटा अनौठो राक्षसी आकृति ठड्याइन्छ । त्यसका तीनवटा खुट्टा हुन्छन् । शरीर विशाल छ । अनि साँझ परेपछि त्यही आकृतिलाई टोलवासीले घिसार्दै दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् र आगो लगाएर जलाउँछन् । काठमाडौँमा वर्सेनि देखिने यो दृश्य गथाँमुगः पर्वको हो । गथाँमुगः पर्व अहिले गैर नेवार समुदायबीच गठेमंगलको नामले परिचित भइरहेको छ । गथाँमुगः काठमाडौं उपत्यकाको नेवार समुदायको महत्वपूर्ण सांस्कृतिक पर्व हो ।

यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको एउटा सबैभन्दा चर्चित किंवदन्ति छ । जुन घण्टाकर्ण नाम गरेको अत्याचारी राक्षससँग सम्बन्धित रहेको छ । किंवदन्ती अनुसार घण्टाकर्ण यति ठूलो अत्याचारी थियो कि बाटो हिँड्ने मानिससँग जबर्जस्ती कर उठाउँथ्यो, दुःख दिन्थ्यो र समाजलाई आतंकित बनाएको थियो । धार्मिक मन्त्र वा पवित्र कुरा सुन्न उसलाई मनै पर्दैन थियो । त्यसैले यस्ता कुरा सुन्न नपरोस् भनेर उसले आफ्ना दुवै कानमा ठूला घण्टा झुन्ड्याएको थियो ।

जब उ हिड्थ्यो ती घण्टा ठूलो आवाज निकालेर बज्थे । त्यसैले उसको नाम नै घण्टाकर्ण रहन गएको विश्वास गरिन्छ । तर यो किंवदन्तिमा पनि ट्वीस्ट आउँछ । एकदिन अत्याचारी घण्टाकर्णको अन्त्य हुन्छ । एक दिन एक चतुर तान्त्रिकले घण्टाकर्णलाई छलपूर्वक दलदलमा फसाउने योजना बनाउँछन् । राक्षस दलदलमा नराम्ररी फस्छ । निस्कन नसकेपछि वर्षौंदेखि उसको आतंक सहिरहेका मानिसहरूले ढुंगा र माटो प्रहार गरेर उसको अन्त्य गरिदिन्छन् । यही सामूहिक विजयको सम्झना र खुशीयालीमा गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने परम्परा शुरु भएको जनविश्वास रहेको छ । त्यसैले हरेक वर्ष श्रावण कृष्ण चतुर्दशीका दिन काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका नेवार समुदायमा गथाँमुगःको बेग्लै रौनक शुरु हुन्छ । काठमाडौं होस्, भक्तपुर होस् वा ललितपु, टोलटोलमा यसको छुट्टै चहलपहल देखिन्छ । घरका ढोकामा फलामको औंठी वा अन्य सुरक्षात्मक वस्तु राख्ने, घर सफा गर्ने, चोकमा राक्षसको आकृति बनाउने तथा विभिन्न परम्परागत विधि पूरा गर्ने चलन छ । कतिपय स्थानमा बालबालिका र युवाहरू घरघरमा गएर सहयोग वा दान संकलन गर्छन् ।

कतै परम्परागत गीत, बाजागाजा र सांस्कृतिक गतिविधिले उपत्यकाको वातावरणलाई थप जीवन्त र सांस्कृतिक बनाउँछ । यो पर्व मनाउने क्रममा दिनभर तयार गरिएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतीकात्मक आकृतिलाई साँझतिर टोलवासी मिलेर तानेर दोबाटोसम्म पु¥याउँछन् । त्यसपछि विधिपूर्वक त्यसलाई जलाइन्छ । यसरी जलाइएको घण्टाकर्णको प्रतिक पर्वको निरन्तरताको रुपमा मात्रै रहेको छैन । यसको सांकेतिक अर्थ खराब शक्तिमाथि असल शक्तिको विजयको प्रतीक पनि हो । रोगव्याधि, भूतप्रेत, अशुभ शक्ति र नकारात्मक ऊर्जा घर तथा समाजबाट टाढा जाओस् भन्ने धार्मिक विश्वास पनि यो पर्वसँग जोडिएको छ । गथाँमुगः पर्व मनाउने क्रममा काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका टोल बस्तीहरूमा यसको आफ्नै स्थानीय शैली र परम्परा भेटिन्छ ।

काठमाडौंका पुराना नेवारी टोलदेखि भक्तपुरका ऐतिहासिक बस्ती र ललितपुरका परम्परागत चोकसम्म गथाँमुगःले उपत्यकाको साझा सांस्कृतिक सम्पदालाई जिवित राखेको छ । आजको आधुनिक काठमाडौँमा इन्टरनेट, मोबाइल, सामाजिक सञ्जाल र व्यस्त जीवनशैलीबीच पनि अमूल्य निधिका रुपमा रहेका यस्ता जात्रा तथा पर्वहरुले निरन्तरता पाइरहेका छन् । त्यसैले हरेक जात्रा वा पर्वजस्तै गथाँमुगःको दिन साँझपख काठमाडौँका नेवारी वस्ती वा चोकमा घण्टाकर्णको आकृति आगोमा जलिरहेको देख्न पाइन्छ । यही कारण सयौँ वर्ष पुरानो यो परम्परा आज पनि काठमाडौं उपत्यकाका गल्ली गल्लीमा उस्तै जीवन्त छ ।

articles.title: राडारमा गंगा, भानु र प्रकाश, देउवा–प्रचण्डका स्वकीयविरुद्ध अख्तियारको अनुसन्धान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । अख्तियार सक्रिय बनेको छ। स–साना मुद्दामा अल्झिने गरेको अख्तियार पछिल्लो समय ठूला भनिएकाहरुसम्म पुग्ने प्रयास गरिरहेको छ। रत, अख्तियारले चालेका यस्ता कदमहरु कति सफल वा असफल त्यसको लेखाजोखा छुट्टे होला तर, शंका लागेका र आरोप खेपेकामाथिको अनुसन्धान हघि बढ्दा यसको प्रभावकारितामाथिका चासोहरु बढेका छन् ।

अख्तियार दुरुपयोग अनुसन्धान आयोगले दुईजना पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्रीहरुका स्वकीय सचिव र पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री आरजु राणा देउवाका पूर्वसहयोगीमाथि अनुसन्धान अघि बढाएको छ । अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री शेरबहादुर देउवाका स्वकिय सचिव भानु देउवा र पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री प्रचण्डकी छोरी समेत रहेकी स्वकिय सचिव गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ ।

यतिमात्रै नभई अख्तियारले पूर्वपरराष्ट्रमन्त्री तथा देउवा पत्नी आरजु राणा देउवाका सहयोगी समेत रहेका सुदूरपश्चिम प्रदेशसभाका सदस्य प्रकाश बहादुर देउवामाथि पनि अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। जसमध्ये प्रकाश अहिले पनि अमेरिकामै रहेका छन्। प्रकाश आरजुको निकट सहयोगी रहेको बताइन्छ भने उनी २०७९ मा सम्पन्न प्रदेशसभा निर्वाचनमा कैलाली क्षेत्र नम्बर–५ (२) बाट प्रदेश सभामा निर्वाचित भएका थिए । उनी २०७९ माघमा प्रदेशको भौतिक पूर्वाधार विकास मन्त्री बनेका थिए । प्रकाश र भानु दुबै देउवाका भतिजहरु हुन्।

अनुसन्धान जारी

अख्तियारले तीनजनाविरुद्ध नै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र भ्रष्टाचारसम्बन्धि कसुरमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको बताइन्छ। प्रकाशविरुद्ध पूर्वमन्त्री समेत भइसकेकाले भ्रष्टाचार र सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरण र गंगा र भानुविरुद्ध भने सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको अनुसन्धान चलिरहेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ ।

प्रकाश देउवाविरुद्धको अनुसन्धान कसरी ?

प्रकाश देउवा अहिले अमेरिकामा छन्। उपचारका लागि भन्दै अमेरिका पुगेका प्रकाश अहिलेसम्म नेपाल फर्किएका छैनन्। उनी प्रदेश सांसद समेत भएपनि लामो समय संसदमा अनुपस्थित रहँदै आएका छन्। धेरैले उनको सेवा सुविधा नै कटौति हुनुपर्ने माग गरिरहेको बेला प्रदेश संसद सचिवालयले यसबारे थप बुझ्ने काम भइरहेकोबाहेक जवाफ दिने गरेको देखिन्न। भने तलव रोक्का गर्ने प्रावधान नै नरहेको भन्ने गरेको छ। यता, अख्तियारले पनि प्रकाश अमेरिकामा भएकोबाहेक सूचना प्राप्त गर्न सकेको देखिन्न। उनीविरुद्ध अख्तियारले अनुसन्धानका निम्ति फारम भराउने गरि तयारी गरिरहेको बताइन्छ ।

भानु देउवा र गंगा दाहालविरुद्ध के हुँदैछ ?

भानु र गंगाबारे अनुसन्धान गर्न सम्पत्ति शुद्धीकरण अनुसन्धान विभागले पत्राचार गरेको अख्तियारले जनाएको छ। एकहप्ताअघि मात्रै सम्पत्ति शुद्धिकरणको पत्र प्राप्त गरेको अख्तियारको दाबी छ। योसंगै अख्तियारले विभिन्न विभागमा उनीहरुको सम्पत्ति विवरण माग गर्दै पत्राचार समेत गरिसकेको बताइएको छ। सम्पत्ति विवरण संकलनपश्चात मात्रै उनीहरुलाई सम्पत्ति सम्बन्धि फारम भराउने र बयान लिने काम थाल्ने अख्तियारको जिकिर छ । यता, अख्तियारका अधिकारीहरुले उनीहरुको बैंक विवरण र कारोबारको विवरण एकीकृत गरिरहेको समेत बताइन्छ।

केपी ओलीका स्वकियविरुद्ध पनि अनुसन्धान

अख्तियारले पूर्वप्रधानमन्त्री केपी ओलीका स्वकिय राजेश बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको छ। गएको जेठ अन्तिम सातादेखि अनुसन्धान शुरु गरेको अख्तियारले के गरिरहेको छ भन्ने प्रगति विवरण सार्वजनिक रुपमा दिने गरेको छैन् ।

बज्राचार्यले अकुत सम्पत्ति आर्जन गरेको आरोपमा अनुसन्धान गरिरहेको अख्तियारले उनलाई फारम भराउनेदेखि बयान लिने काम समेत गरिसकेको बताइन्छ। बज्राचार्यले सम्पत्ति विवरण सम्बन्धी १३ पन्ने फारम भरेर अख्तियारमा बुझाइ सकेका छन् । बज्राचार्यविरुद्ध यति समूहको थामसेर्कु ट्रेकिङले दरबारमार्गस्थित नेपाल ट्रस्टको जग्गा लिजमा लैजादा अनियमितता गरेको आरोप छ। बज्राचार्यकी पत्नी रश्मि शाक्यले यति समूहबाट बालकोटस्थित रोज भिलेज हाउजिङभित्रको झण्डै चार आना जग्गामा बनेको घर घुस बापत लिएको केन्द्रीय अनुसन्धान ब्यूरो (सीआईबी)को अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्ष छ । यहि विवरण देखाउदै सीआइबीले नै अख्तियारलाई लेखि पठाएपछि अनुसन्धान अघि बढिरहेको छ । उसोतः सम्पत्ति विवरणमाथि अनुसन्धान गर्दा गैरकानुनी रूपमा आर्जन गरेको भेटिएमा आयोगले भ्रष्टाचार निवारण ऐन २०५९ अनुसार विशेष अदालतमा मुद्दा दायर गर्न सक्ने कानुनी व्यवस्था छ । अहिले आयोगले गरिरहेको अनुसन्धानको निष्कर्षपछि मात्रै अभियोजन हुने नहुने विषय टुंगो लाग्नेछ।

अख्तियारमाथि भरोसा कि प्रश्न ?

अख्तियारले गरिरहेका अनुसन्धान र अभियोजन कति प्रतिशत अदालतबाट प्रमाणित हुन्छन्? पछिल्लो समय यो प्रश्न उठिरहेको छ। अख्तियारले अभियोजनलाई कर्मकाण्डी बनाउने गरेको आरोप समेत लाग्ने गरेको छ। यस्तोमा अख्तियारले अभियोजनका लागि समय लिएपनि परिपक्क अनुसन्धान गर्नुपर्ने र अभियोजनमा समेत विशेष ध्यान दिनुपर्ने बताइन्छ। तर, अख्तियारमाथि कार्यपालिकाको हस्तक्षेपका कारण पनि अनुसन्धान प्रभावकारी हुनेमा शंका भने देखिन्छ। तर, अख्तियारले आफ्नो शाख जोगाउने र गैरकानूनी सम्पत्ति आर्जन र भ्रष्टाचार नियन्त्रणमा उल्लेख्य भूमिका खेल्नुपर्ने संवैधानिक व्यवस्थाको पालना कसरी गर्छ भन्ने प्रश्न र भरोसा कायमै देखिन्छ।

articles.title: याडियाका तीन नयाँ स्मार्ट विद्युतीय स्कुटर नेपाली बजारमा, १० हजार छुटको अफर
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । नेपालका लागि याडिया (YADEA) को आधिकारिक वितरक कुजु नेपाल प्रा. लि. ले नयाँ पुस्ताका GS70, GT70 र GTM90 विद्युतीय स्कुटरहरू नेपाली बजारमा औपचारिक रूपमा सार्वजनिक गरेको छ। आधुनिक प्रविधि, उत्कृष्ट कार्यक्षमता र नेपाली सडक अनुकूल डिजाइन गरिएका यी स्कुटरहरूले दैनिक सहरी यात्रादेखि लामो दूरीको यात्रासम्मका फरक-फरक आवश्यकता पूरा गर्ने कम्पनीको भनाइ छ।

सार्वजनिक गरिएका तीन मोडेलमध्ये GS70 लाई दैनिक सहरी यात्राका लागि किफायती विकल्पका रूपमा तयार पारिएको छ। यसमा २.१ kWh LFP ब्याट्री र २.८ kW पिक मोटर दिइएको छ, जसले एकपटकको पूर्ण चार्जमा १०५ किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज प्रदान गर्छ। लामो दूरीको यात्रा गर्नेहरूका लागि GT70 उपयुक्त छ, जसमा ५.७ kWh को डुअल LFP ब्याट्री (३.६ kWh फिक्स्ड र २.१ kWh रिमुभेबल) तथा ३.७ kW पिक मोटर रहेको छ। यसले २२० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ भने रिमुभेबल ब्याट्रीका कारण घर वा कार्यालयमा सहजै चार्ज गर्न सकिन्छ। प्रिमियम श्रेणीको GTM90 मा ३.६ kWh लिथियम ब्याट्री र ५ kW पिक मोटर जडान गरिएको छ, जसले ८० किमि प्रतिघण्टाको उच्च गति र १५० किलोमिटरसम्मको रेन्ज दिन्छ।

प्रविधि र सुरक्षाका हिसाबले यी नयाँ स्कुटरहरू निकै आधुनिक छन्। ती सबैमा TFT स्मार्ट डिस्प्ले, ब्लुटुथ कनेक्टिभिटी, मोबाइल नेभिगेसन मिररिङ, याडिया स्मार्ट एप, कि-लेस प्रणाली र ५ जनासम्म प्रयोग गर्न मिल्ने 'फ्यामिली सेयरिङ' सुविधा उपलब्ध छ। यात्रालाई थप सुरक्षित र सहज बनाउन ट्र्याक्सन कन्ट्रोल सिस्टम (TCS), क्रुज कन्ट्रोल, हिल होल्ड, हिल डिसेन्ट कन्ट्रोल र डुअल डिस्क ब्रेकजस्ता अत्याधुनिक प्रविधि समावेश गरिएका छन्।

कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलका ब्याट्रीमा ३ वर्ष वा ५०,००० किलोमिटरसम्मको दीर्घकालीन वारेन्टी प्रदान गरेको छ। हाल यी स्कुटरहरू देशभर रहेका २० वटा आधिकारिक याडिया डिलरशिपहरू मार्फत उपलब्ध छन्। साथै, सार्वजनिक गरिएको अवसरमा नाइमा अटो शो (NAIMA Auto Show) सम्म लागू हुने गरी कम्पनीले तीनै मोडेलमा रु. १०,००० को विशेष नगद छुट दिएको छ। ग्राहकहरूले नजिकैको शोरुममा गई टेस्ट राइड तथा फाइनान्सिङ सुविधाबारे थप जानकारी लिन सक्नेछन्।

articles.title: खल्तीबाट डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा दैनिक १ लाख र बम्परमा १० लाख जित्न सकिने
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । आईएमई खल्ती लिमिटेडले अर्थ मन्त्रालयअन्तर्गतको आन्तरिक राजस्व विभागद्वारा सञ्चालित ‘करदाता प्रोत्साहन उपहार कार्यक्रम, २०८३’ मा आफ्ना प्रयोगकर्तालाई सहभागी गराउने भएको छ। खल्तीमार्फत रु १०० भन्दा बढीको योग्य डिजिटल भुक्तानी गर्दा ग्राहकहरू स्वतः दैनिक तथा पाक्षिक उपहार छनोटमा सहभागी हुनेछन्।

यस कार्यक्रमअन्तर्गत दैनिक एक जना विजेताले कर कट्टीपछि रु. १ लाख र प्रत्येक १५ दिनमा एक जना बम्पर विजेताले रु १० लाख प्राप्त गर्नेछन्। भुक्तानीको विवरण सुरक्षित रूपमा राजस्व विभागको प्रणालीमा पुग्ने र उपहार कुपन स्वतः सिर्जना भई खल्ती एपमै देखिने व्यवस्था मिलाइएको छ। विभागले प्रत्येक महिनाको १ र १६ गते स्वचालित प्रणालीबाट विजेता छनोट गरी एसएमएस, इमेल तथा खल्तीमार्फत जानकारी गराउनेछ।

बिलमा आधारित कारोबार प्रवर्द्धन गरी डिजिटल अर्थतन्त्र र राष्ट्रिय राजस्व प्रणालीलाई सुदृढ बनाउने लक्ष्यका साथ यो सहकार्य गरिएको आईएमई खल्तीका प्रमुख कार्यकारी अधिकृत प्रवीण रेग्मीले बताएका छन्।

articles.title: सर्वसाधारणको रकम गरिमा विकास बैंकले झ्वाम पार्दै, झ्वाम पार्ने को–को ?
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । के तपाईंको गरिमा विकास बैंकमा खाता छ ?के तपाईंले आफुले मेहेनत गरेको रकम गरिमा बिकास बैंकमा राख्नु भएको छ ? यदी छ भने तपाईंका लागि आज दुखको खबर छ । कारण हो, ग्राहकले राखेको रकम बैंकको भवन किन्दा अपचलन गरेर प्रचलित मूल्यभन्दा बढी मूल्यामा किनिएको छ । प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन र प्रचलित बजार मूल्यलाई समेत लत्याउँदै बैंक व्यवस्थापनले ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरेको छ । सर्वसाधारणले दुःख गरेर बैंकमा जम्मा गरेको निक्षेप सुरक्षित छ त?भन्ने प्रश्न पनि उठिरहेको छ ।

गरिमा विकास बैंकले काठमाडौँको बालुवाटारमा ३७ आनाभन्दा बढी जग्गा र त्यसमा बनेको घर खरिद गर्दा प्रचलित बजार मूल्य र स्वयं प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनलाई समेत लत्याउँदै करिब ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी मूल्य तिरिएको भेटिएको छ। बजार मन्दीमा रहेका बेला प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन भन्दा दोब्बर मूल्य हालेर जग्गा र भवन किनिएको छ ।

काठमाडौंको बालुवाटारमा कित्ता नम्बर ४९ मा रहेको २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसा अर्थात् ३७ दशमलव २६ आना जग्गा र ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिटको बनेको यो आरसीसी भवन शिखर इन्स्योरेन्सका पूर्वअध्यक्ष राजेन्द्रप्रसाद श्रेष्ठको २०८२ सालमा गरिमा विकास बैंकले केन्द्रीय कार्यालय बनाउन खरिद ग¥यो ।

बैंकले यो जग्गा खरिद गर्दा प्रतिआना १ करोड ५६ लाख १४ हजार ९२२ रुपैयाँ तिरेको देखिन्छ । अर्थात २ रोपनी ५ आना १ पैसाको जग्गाको मूल्या ५८ करोड १८ लाख १२ हजार रुपैयाँ बैकलाई पर्न गयो। अब यही जग्गामा रहेको यो भवनको क्षेत्रफल ४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट रहेको छ ।

बैंकले यो भवनको मूल्य ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरेको देखिन्छ । वर्गफिटमा हिसाब गर्दा पनि प्रति वर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँमा खरिद गरको छ । तपाईलाई यो खरिद मूल्य सायद सामान्य नै लाग्यो होला? यो सामान्य घरजग्गा किनबेच देखिए तापनि, प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बैंकको हालेको रकम जुधाउँदा भने ठूलो अन्तर देखिन्छ ।

प्राविधिक प्रतिवेदन र बजार मूल्यको वास्तविकता

पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले बैंक धितोकै लागि तयार पारेको प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदन अनुसार सो क्षेत्रमा जग्गाको स्थानीय बजार दर प्रतिआना ८० लाख रुपैयाँ मात्र छ। स्थानीय व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार पनि बजारको अधिकतम मूल्य ९० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी पर्दैन।

प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कन प्रतिवेदनमा सडकको अधिकार क्षेत्र कट्टा गरी कायम भएको १ रोपनी १३ आना ३ पैसा जग्गाको कुल बजार मूल्य १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार मात्रै कायम गरेको छ । पृथक इन्जिनियरिङ कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कमर्सियल भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको २३ करोड ८३ लाख ९९ हजार यो जग्गाको मूल्या कायम गरेको छ । फेयर मार्केट भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भनेको १७ करोड ७० लाख ९८ हजार कायम गर्यो ।

डिस्ट्रेस भ्यालु अनुसार मूल्याङ्कनको निष्कर्ष भने १४ करोड १६ लाख ७८ हजार कन्सल्टेन्ट्सले कायम गरेको छ । तर बंैकले बैंकले भने सोही जग्गालाई ५८ करोड १८ लाखभन्दा बढी भुक्तानी गर्यो। यो खेल जग्गामा मात्र रोकिएन, भवन खरिदमा पनि उस्तै अस्वाभाविक मूल्या हालियो ।

४७ हजार ६ सय २१ वर्गफिट क्षेत्रफल रहेको सो भवनको मूल्य बैंकले ३९ करोड ३१ लाख ८८ हजार रुपैयाँ तय गरेर खरिद ग¥यो। अर्थात् प्रतिवर्गफिट ८ हजार २ सय ५६ रुपैयाँ! निर्माण व्यवसायीहरूका अनुसार काठमाडौँमा अत्यन्त लक्जरियस सामग्री प्रयोग गर्दा पनि नयाँ भवन निर्माण खर्च प्रतिवर्गफिट अधिकतम ४ हजारदेखि ६ हजार रुपैयाँसम्म मात्र पुग्छ। प्रतिवर्गफिट ६ हजार नै मान्ने हो भने पनि २८ करोड ५७ लाख पर्ने भवनलाई बैंकले १० करोड ७४ लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी अतिरिक्त मूल्य हालेर किनेको देखिन्छ ।

जग्गामा २४ करोड ६५ लाख र घरमा १० करोड ७४ लाख गरी कुल ३५ करोड ४० लाख रुपैयाँभन्दा बढी रकम बजार मूल्य र प्राविधिक मूल्याङ्कनभन्दा बढी मूल्य हालिएको छ । घर–जग्गा बजारमा मन्दी छाएका बेला प्रचलित भाउभन्दा निकै माथि गएर गरिएको यो निर्णयमा गरिमा विकास बैंकका सञ्चालक अनिल रेग्मी, ईश्वरीप्रसाद ढकाल र सीईओ माधवप्रसाद उपाध्याय लगायतको भूमिका देखिन्छ ।

सर्वसाधारण निक्षेपकर्ताको पसिनाको कमाईमाथि बैंकका सञ्चालक र उच्च व्यवस्थापनबाट भएको यो अस्वाभाविक खर्चले बैंकको संस्थागत सुशासन र नियमनकारी निकाय नेपाल राष्ट्र बैंकको अनुगमनमाथि ठूलो प्रश्न खडा गरेको छ।

articles.title: फोनिज काठमाडौँको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा पदयात्रा सम्पन्न
articles.summary:
काठमाडौँ । नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिको आयोजनामा वृक्षरोपण तथा फोनिज पदयात्रा सम्पन्न भएको छ ।

फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसको अवसर पारेर आज शनिवार काठमाडौँको साँखु–बज्रयोगिनी हुँदै मणिचूड दहसम्म पदयात्रा तथा विभिन्न गुम्बा तथा मन्दिर परिसरमा वृक्षरोपण गरेका हुन् । काठमाडौँ जिल्ला अन्तरगत फोनिज आवद्ध प्रतिनिधिहरू, स्थानीय जनप्रतिनिधि र विभिन्न जातिय संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधिहरूको उल्लेख्य सहभागितामा साँखुमा भेला भइ बज्रयोगिनी मन्दिर परिसरबाट करिव १७ किलोमिटिरको दूरीमा पदयात्रा गरेका थिए ।

पदयात्रापछि मणिचूड दहमा भएको औपचारिक कार्यक्रममा विभिन्न वक्ताहरूले धार्मिक पर्यटन प्रवद्र्धन र संरक्षणमा आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको महत्वपूर्ण भूमिका रहेको बताएका छन् । कार्यक्रममा बोल्दै शंकरापुर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का अध्यक्ष पोते थिङले मणिचूड दहको महत्वबारे प्रकाश पार्दै प्रचारप्रसारको अभाव तथा राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज वन क्षेत्रको निश्चित मापदण्डका कारण अझै ओझेलमा परेको बताए । मणिचूड दह र त्यस क्षेत्रमा रहेका हरेक धार्मिक तथा साँस्कृतिक सम्पदाको संरक्षण र प्रवद्र्धनका साथै थप व्यवस्थापन गर्न वनसंग जोडिएको कानुनलाई परिमार्जण गर्नुपर्ने धारणा राखे ।

त्यस्तै शिवपुरी नागार्जुन राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्ज मध्यवर्ती क्षेत्र व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष श्यामकुमार वाइबाले निकुञ्जभित्र रहेको मणिचूड दह बौद्ध र हिन्दू दुवै धर्मालम्बीहरू पवित्र तिर्थस्थलको रूपमा मान्दै आएको बताए । विशेष गरि जनजातिजातिको बहुल्यता रहेको त्यस क्षेत्रमा बौद्ध धर्मालम्बीहरूले विभिन्न समयमा पूजापाठ, मोन्लाम लगायत साउन महिने जलयात्रा, जनैपूर्णिमा लगायत साँस्कृतिक पर्वहरू मनाउने भएकोले थप महत्व रहेको बताए । अहिले निकुञ्ज, स्थानीय तह र मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिबीचको समन्वयमा व्यवस्थित बनाउने रणनीति रहेको बताए ।

कार्यक्रममा राष्ट्रि शहिद तथा शान्ति स्मारक पार्क र गोकर्ण यज्ञडोल सामुदायिक वन उपभोक्त समितिका अध्यक्ष सुर्दशन सिग्देलले वन, जंगल, जल र जमिनको संरक्षणमा जनजाति समुदायको उल्लेख्य भूमिका रहेको बताउँदै आफ्नो साँस्कृतिक पहिचान र अधिकारसँग जाडिएको क्षेत्रमा राज्यले दुःख दिन नहुने बताए । जनजाति समुदायले विशेष गरि प्रकृतिको पुजा गर्ने चाडपर्वलाई साँस्कृतिक पहिचानको रूपमा विश्वमाझ चिनाउन सफल रहेको बताउँदै राष्ट्रिय शहिद पार्क वन क्षेत्रमा समेत विभन्नि जातजातिको अस्तित्व समेट्ने गरि भिलेजग्रामको निर्माण गरिएको बताए ।

फोनिज बागमति प्रदेश समितिका महासचिव राजु नापितले फोनिजले पत्रकारितालाई आफ्नो पेसागत हकअधिकारमात्र नभएर भाषा, कला, संस्कृतिको संरक्षण र सम्वद्र्धनमा विशेष योगदान पु¥याउँदै आइरहेको बताए । फोनिज बागमति प्रदेशभित्र पत्रकारहरूलाई एकीकृत गराउँदै समुदायको पहिचान र अधिकार सुनिश्चित गराउन समेत जिल्लासमितिहरूले सक्रियतापूर्वक गतिविधि सञ्चालन गराउँदै आएको बताए ।

त्यस्तै फोनिज संघीय समितिका सचिव सुनिल महर्जनले फोनिज पदयात्राले रमाइलो मात्र नभइ अनुसन्धानका आयाम बुझ्न पाएको बताए । मणिचूडको सुन्दर ऐतिहासिक धार्मिक पर्यटकीय स्थल प्रकृतिप्रेमी र आध्यात्मिक शान्ति चाहनेहरूका लागि विशेष रहने बताउँदै पत्रकारिताको माध्यमबाट प्रचारप्रसारलाई तिब्रता दिनुपर्ने बताए । फोनिजले नेपालभित्र रहेका आदिवासी जनजाति समुदायसंग जोडिएका कला, भाषा, धर्म संस्कृति र पहिचान बोकेका विषयवस्तुहरूको अध्ययन र अनुसन्धान गरि विश्वसामु चिनाउने प्रयास गरिरहेको बताए ।

नेपाल आदिवासी जनजाति पत्रकार महासंघ (फोनिज) काठमाडौँ जिल्ला समितिका अध्यक्ष भिमबहादुर लामाले सामाजिक एकता र सद्भाव कायम उद्देश्यका साथ फोनिजको २७ औँ स्थापना दिवसलाई सार्थक पार्न पदयात्रा तथा वृक्षरोपण कार्यक्रमको आयोजना गरिएको बताए । उनले जनजाति पत्रकारहरूको पेसागत क्षमतालाई दरिलो बनाउन अध्ययन, अनुसन्धान र आलेख लेखनमा सहयोग पु¥याउने उद्देश्यले धार्मिक पर्यटकीय क्षेत्र तथा जनजाति समुदायको साँस्कृतिक तथा धार्मिक महत्व बोकेको क्षेत्र साँखु, बज्रयोगिनी र मणिचूड दहको यात्रा तय गरेको बताए । राज्य र पहुँचवाला समूहहरूबाट आदिवासी जनजातिहरूको थातथालोमा जलविद्युत गुरूयोजनाहरू सञ्चालन गर्ने, विकास निर्माण र राष्ट्रिय निकुञ्जको नाममा परिवारहरू विस्थापित बनाएको अध्यक्ष लामाले आरोप लगाए ।

फोनिज काठमाडौँ जिल्ला कार्यसमितिका सचिव रत्नमान महर्जनले सञ्चालन गरेको कार्यक्रममा नेपाल प्रहरीका पूर्व डिआइजी देउती गुरूङ, गोकर्णेश्वर नगरपालिका वडा नं. ८ का वडा सदस्य सुमन लामा, नेपाल पत्रकार महासंघ काठमाडौँ शाखा उपाध्यक्षद्वाय कमल राना मगर, कान्ति न्यौपाने, सहसचिब बिक्रम रत्न, मणिचूड मन्दिर व्यवस्थापन समितिका अध्यक्ष भिम घ्लान, नेपाल बौद्ध धर्म संरक्षण संघका महासचिव उमा गुरूङ, साँस्कृतिक युवा समूहका अध्यक्ष वेचन लामा, समाजसेवी किरण मोक्तान, सोफिया पाख्रिन लगायत अतिथि रहेका थिए । पदयात्रामा फोनिजकर्मी तथा विभिन्न संघसंस्थाका प्रतिनिधि गरि ६८ जनाको सहभागीता रहेको थियो ।

articles.title: हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्षको बहारः ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान
articles.summary:
काठमाडौं । बाग्मती प्रदेशको राजधानी हेटौँडामा पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ लाई लक्षित गर्दै ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइन लागिएको पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अन्तर्गत सरसफाइ थालिएको हो ।

यो वर्ष बाग्मतीको प्रादेशिक राजधानीस्थित हेटौँडा उपमहानगरपालिकाले पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मनाउँदैछ । पर्यटन वर्षको कार्यक्रम अन्तर्गत सून्य फोहोर अभियान सञ्चालन गरिएको छ । यहि अभियान अन्तर्गत शनिवार हातमा कुचो र बोरा बोकेर जनप्रतिनिधि, सुरक्षाकर्मी, टोल विकास संस्थाका पदाधिकारी र स्थानीयवासी सडकमा निस्किए । हेटौँडाका सडकदेखि टोलसम्म सरसफाइ गर्दै उनीहरूले ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियान शुरु गरेका हुन् ।

फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई केवल सरसफाइ अभियानका रूपमा नभई पर्यटन, वातावरण संरक्षण र नागरिक संस्कृतिसँग जोडिएको दीर्घकालीन अभियानका रूपमा अघि बढाइने योजना उपमहानगरपालिकाको छ । उपमहानगरपालिकाले ‘जाऔँ हेटौंडा, रमाऔँ हेटौंडामा’ भन्ने मूल नारासहित मनाइने पर्यटन वर्ष २०८३ को पहिलो र प्रमुख कार्यक्रमका रूपमा ‘शून्य फोहोर’ अभियान अघि सारिएको हो ।

मुख्य तथा सहायक सडक, सार्वजनिक स्थल र पर्यटकीय क्षेत्रको सरसफाइसँगै वृक्षारोपण र सौन्दर्यीकरणलाई पनि अभियानको प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ । टोल विकास संस्था नगर समन्वय समितिको संयोजनमा सुरु भएको अभियान नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोल विकास संस्थामा सुरु गरिएको छ । पर्यटन वर्षको अवसरमा सुरु गरिएको ‘शून्य फोहोर हेटौँडा’ अभियानले नगरको स्वच्छता र सौन्दर्य कायम राख्दै हेटौँडालाई पर्यटकीय गन्तव्यका रूपमा चिनाउन सहयोग पुग्ने अपेक्षा गरिएको दाबी छ ।

पर्यटन वर्ष–२०८३ मा हेटौँडामा आन्तरिक तथा बाह्य पर्यटकको संख्या बढाउने उपमहानगरपालिकाको लक्ष्य छ । पर्यटकलाई आकर्षित गर्न नयाँ गन्तव्यको प्रचारसँगै शहरको स्वच्छता, सौन्दर्य र व्यवस्थित वातावरणलाई पनि प्राथमिकतामा राखिएको छ ।

यही उद्देश्यले सुरु गरिएको यो अभियानलाई नगरका ३ सय ७७ वटै टोलसम्म विस्तार गरिँदैछ । टोल–टोलमा सरसफाइ र फोहोर व्यवस्थापनलाई प्रभावकारी बनाउँदै हेटौँडालाई स्वच्छ, सुन्दर र पर्यटकमैत्री शहरका रूपमा विकास गर्ने र पर्यटन वर्षमा बढीभन्दा बढी पर्यटक भित्र्याउने लक्ष्य लिइएको छ ।

articles.title: Nepal’s labour market caught between jobless workers and worker shortages
articles.summary:
After spending 18 years working in the United Arab Emirates and Saudi Arabia, Nil Bahadur Khadka of Banke returned to Nepal seven months ago hoping to settle back home.

Armed with certificates proving his skills, he went from one construction company to another looking for work as an overseer. No one hired him.

After nearly seven months without a job, Khadka received a call from his former employer in Saudi Arabia.

“We have secured a new contract in Kuwait. We can offer you the same position with a higher salary. We have already sent a demand letter to a recruitment agency. Go there and submit your passport,” the company told him.

Khadka immediately agreed.

He is now preparing to leave for Kuwait after being assured that he will be able to save around Rs100,000 a month.

“Over there, companies actively seek us out and call us. Here, even after going from door to door looking for work, nobody trusts us,” Khadka told Kantipur. “My children have not finished their education. At a time like this, I cannot just sit idle at home.”

His flight is expected to be booked within a few days.

Thirty-year-old Rupal BK of Dang, who returned from Malaysia just three months ago, has had a similar experience.

“There are no large industries in our area hiring 300 to 400 workers. There are only small companies that employ five to seven. When we approach them, they say they have no vacancies,” BK said. “Labour work is not available all the time. I need at least Rs20,000 to Rs30,000 a month to support my family, but I cannot find a job that pays that much.”

Unable to find reliable work, he too is preparing to leave, this time for Qatar.

“I have found a labour job at a hotel in Qatar,” he said. “They say it will cost me Rs250,000 to go there. I am waiting for my visa.”

While Khadka and BK are preparing to leave the country again because they cannot find work at home, employers complain that they cannot find enough workers.

Shivahari Ghimire, secretary-general of the Federation of Contractors’ Associations of Nepal, estimates that the construction sector alone needs an additional 300,000 to 500,000 workers.

“The construction sector needs 1.1 million workers directly. Only around 800,000 to 900,000 are currently available in the market,” Ghimire said. “A large number of skilled workers have already left the country. We have had to hire workers from Bangladesh and India.”

Nepal’s labour market appears caught in a paradox: citizens cannot find jobs while employers struggle to find the workers they need.

According to the 2021 National Population and Housing Census, 15.7 million people, or 65.5 percent of Nepal’s population, were classified as economically active, or part of the labour force. They included 8.2 million men and 7.5 million women.

The largest age group within the economically active population is 25 to 29, with about 1.9 million people. Another 1.8 million are aged 20 to 24, while around 1.78 million are aged 35 to 39.

Much of this 20-39 age group is searching for productive employment and decent work.

According to the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment, more than 745,000 unemployed people registered with employment service centres established in 746 local units last fiscal year.

Prabal Jung Pandey, chair of the Employers’ Council at the Federation of Nepalese Chambers of Commerce and Industry, said the shortage was particularly acute among skilled workers.

“We can regularly find unskilled workers. But there is a huge shortage of skilled and semi-skilled workers,” Pandey said. “The skilled workers we find are mostly those who have been unable to go abroad for work.”

According to Pandey, construction, hotels and manufacturing are among the sectors facing shortages of skilled workers.

Of Nepal’s employed labour force, the largest share, 57.3 percent, works in the primary sector, including agriculture, forestry and fishing. Another 12.7 percent works in manufacturing and industry, while the remaining 30 percent is employed in services.

A large proportion of skilled workers with experience in construction, manufacturing, hotels and other services are employed abroad.

Nepal does have legal and institutional mechanisms for recognising the skills workers acquire overseas. The National Skill Testing Board, Recognition of Prior Learning system and National Skill Academy Nepal provide mechanisms to assess and certify skills and experience gained abroad.

But many returning workers are unaware of these options. Certificates also have limited recognition in the domestic labour market. Weak coordination with employers means the skills of workers returning from abroad are not being fully utilised.

Forty-three-year-old Arjun Gautam of Bardiya, who returned after 18 years working in the construction sector in Saudi Arabia, said Nepal had not recognised the skills he acquired there.

“I have a certificate for surveying work that I learned in the Gulf. I am proficient in it. I also have a skills certificate issued by the Saudi government,” he said. “But if I want to do the same work here, employers ask for educational certificates, which I do not have.”

Gautam said the failure to recognise his skills had reduced him to the status of a labourer in Nepal.

Pandey said the government and employers needed to carry out comprehensive “skill mapping” to identify the workers available in the country.

“We should record the skills of workers returning from foreign employment at the airport itself,” he said. “Only after skill mapping can we find the workers we need.”

For some, the problem begins even before they leave the country.

Ayush Upadhyay of Dodhara-Chandani in Kanchanpur, who is considering foreign employment, said he had few opportunities in Nepal to acquire practical skills for running a business. Even as he runs his own canteen and hotel in Dodhara-Chandani, he feels he needs to better his skills for potential employment abroad.

The labour ministry established the National Vocational Training Academy Development Committee in December 2023, saying it would produce skilled, competitive and entrepreneurial workers to meet demand in both domestic and international labour markets.

The committee has developed training programmes in various trades, with courses lasting six months or at least 730 working hours. The programmes also have international recognition.

Yet the academy has struggled to produce workers with the skills sought by private employers.

Ramesh Prasad Bakhati, a former executive director of the committee, said training centres were not sufficiently connected to actual labour market demand and that closer coordination with the private sector was essential.

“We cannot prepare workers according to the needs of the private sector without taking the private sector into confidence,” he said. “At present, federal, provincial and local governments are conducting training programmes independently. People who take such training often fail to find jobs.”

Bakhati said procedures for testing and certifying the skills of workers returning from foreign employment had also yet to be approved.

Unemployed workers have limited access to up-to-date information on where jobs are available, how many workers different sectors need and which skills are in growing demand.

The labour ministry established employment service centres at the local level in 2018 to collect and manage labour market information, connect employers with workers and provide support to unemployed people.

Young people across the country have been registering at the centres, hoping to find work based on their qualifications and skills. But only 28,346 of those registered have been given jobs through local government projects, for a maximum of 83 days.

Other businesses and institutions operating at the local level have done little to provide jobs through the system.

Meanwhile, about 51 percent of employment service centres do not even have an information technology-based registration system. Among centres that do, many report using the system only partially.

The ministry has plans to develop a national labour market information system, but it has yet to become fully operational.

According to ministry spokesperson Pitambar Ghimire, the government is trying to develop the “Shram Sansar” platform into a national employment information system. But limited participation by both employers and workers, weak digital capacity at employment service centres and poor management of labour market data have prevented the system from delivering the expected results.

The Shram Sansar portal has been operating for two years. A total of 2,558 employers have registered on the platform and can post their demand for workers. On the other hand, 125,057 unemployed people have registered in search of jobs.

Only 78 of them have found job placements.

An ILO report titled Evaluation of Public Employment Services and Labour Market Policies in Nepal, released on January 16, 2026, identified weak coordination and engagement with employers as one of the main obstacles to effective public employment services.

“Sixty-three percent of employment service centres do not register any type of job vacancy,” the report said. “Where vacancies are registered, most are from the public sector.”

The report said this underscored the need to win the confidence of private-sector employers, bring them into the system and expand services tailored to their needs.

Binod Shrestha, chair of the Joint Trade Union Coordination Centre, said connecting workers with the right skills to jobs offering fair wages remained a major challenge.

“The real gap is not between workers and employers. The problem is the mismatch between the labour market system, workers’ skills, wages and the information available about jobs,” he said.

“Until skilled workers receive fair wages, employers will continue to complain that they cannot find workers, while workers will continue to say they cannot find jobs and head abroad.”

Minister for Youth, Labour and Employment Ramjee Yadav said the government was focusing on jobs and skills development to make Nepali youth more self-reliant and competitive over the next decade.

He said the government had given top priority to the “Employment Promotion Decade”, covering fiscal years 2026-27 to 2036-37.

“The goal is to create enough opportunities at home and engage young people in nation-building,” Yadav told Parliament on Monday. “Employment service centres at the local level have now been transformed into employment, skills and entrepreneurship centres to connect young people with entrepreneurship.”

But while the minister promoted the government’s plans, 27-year-old Anita Urao of Itahari said she had been unable to find work that matched her experience.

“I want to work in sales. I have experience working at clothing and shoe shops,” Urao said. “I registered on Shram Sansar looking for work, but no one contacted me. I also applied for jobs advertised there, but I was never called for an interview.

“Unless you know someone, nobody trusts you.”

articles.title: Non-domestic goods dominate Nepal’s exports as high-value products struggle
articles.summary:
Nepal’s export of high-value goods grew by just 3.16 percent in the last fiscal year compared to the previous fiscal data, sharply contrasting with overall export growth of 13.81 percent during the period.

Exports of products listed under the Nepal Trade Integrated Strategy (NTIS) 2023 reached Rs104.62 billion in the last fiscal year, up marginally from Rs101.41 billion in the fiscal 2024-25.

The government identifies these products as having high export potential and has sought to promote them to diversify exports and boost foreign exchange earnings.

The government introduced the revised NTIS 2023, replacing the NTIS 2016, to boost exports and support Nepal’s graduation from the least developed country category. But three years into its implementation, exports of several identified products have continued to underperform.

Lack of coordination among government agencies, frequent changes in bureaucrats and ministers, policy shifts and political instability have hindered the implementation of NTIS, discouraging investment, productivity and exports of the listed goods, according to industry representatives.

Nepal’s overall export growth, meanwhile, has been dominated by goods the country does not produce domestically. Government data show that much of the increase has been driven by edible oil. According to the Department of Customs, Nepal exported goods worth Rs315.29 billion in the last fiscal year ended mid-July. Edible oil exports accounted for Rs146 billion. Nepali traders import crude edible oil and re-export the processed product to India, taking advantage of tariff concessions under the South Asian Free Trade Area regime.

Private-sector representatives say Nepal needs production- and industry-focused policies, along with legal reforms, to increase productivity and strengthen exports.

“Despite a good concept and policy, the goods listed in NTIS have not been able to grow as expected mainly due to lack of coordination,” said Birendra Raj Pandey, president of the Confederation of Nepalese Industries.

He said the government is preparing industrial development policies and that reforms to some legal provisions could help increase productivity, particularly under a stable government.

“The share of GDP from manufacturing is declining and it needs to be reversed,” Pandey said. Low industrial capacity utilisation and a slowdown in economic activity have hurt production, he added, arguing that increased capital spending and other forms of investment could help revive economic activity.

Nepal has been producing many of the NTIS-listed goods for years, but their production methods and markets have changed little, Pandey said. “The product and market both need to be diversified for market expansion. We need to produce goods that have a competitive advantage compared to our neighbouring countries.”

Among the NTIS-listed products, exports of carpet, tea, iron and steel products, cement, handmade paper and spices declined during the review period.

Carpet exports fell 3.63 percent to Rs10.38 billion, with 367,454 square metres shipped during the year. Traders said the imposition of value-added tax on carpets and raw materials has made Nepali carpets more expensive in the Chinese market, hurting exports.

The government’s National Strategic Work Plan for Carpet Export (2026-2031) aims to modernise the industry, upgrade workers’ skills, introduce computer-based design systems, promote the use of domestic raw materials and expand export markets through digital marketing and e-commerce.

Tea exports fell 13.36 percent to Rs3.98 billion, with 13,303 tonnes exported. Repeated disruptions at the Indian border hurt shipments after India introduced stricter measures, including mandatory laboratory testing, to protect its domestic tea industry amid rising imports. The measures halted Nepali tea exports for more than a month in May and forced some factories to shut for a week in June.

Exports of iron and steel products plunged 62.43 percent to Rs6.14 billion. Shipments to India have fallen sharply since New Delhi imposed safeguard duties on selected steel products, raising concerns over export earnings and jobs.

India imposed a three-year safeguard duty in December last year, ranging from 11 percent to 12 percent on selected steel products. The levy is 12 percent in the first year, 11.5 percent in the second and 11 percent in the third. The measure applies to imports from China, Vietnam and Nepal, while specialty products such as stainless steel are exempt.

Cement exports to India fell 8 percent to Rs2 billion. Delays in issuing or renewing Bureau of Indian Standards certification have repeatedly obstructed shipments of Nepali cement, traders say.

Spices exports plunged 85 percent to Rs147 million, with Nepal exporting 1,689 tonnes of cinnamon, coriander, cumin and turmeric.

Exports of several other NTIS-listed products including yarn, readymade garments, jute and jute products, felt, large cardamom, pashmina, footwear, fabric, dog chews, medicinal herbs, rosin and resin acid, lentils, ginger, vegetables and fruits, coffee, jewellery, pasta and honey, however, increased during the year.

Yarn exports increased 8.79 percent to Rs15.66 billion, with 55,200 tonnes shipped, mostly to India and Turkey.

Readymade garment exports rose 6.27 percent to Rs9.3 billion, with 15.52 million pieces exported.

Jute and jute product exports increased 25.98 percent to Rs10.78 billion, while felt exports rose 16.2 percent to Rs5.97 billion.

Large cardamom exports jumped 64.61 percent to Rs12.64 billion, the highest value recorded, with 6,395 tonnes shipped. The increase has been attributed to tighter global supplies, stable prices and sustained demand in South Asian and Middle Eastern markets. India remains the dominant buyer, accounting for around 99 percent of Nepal’s exports, with the spice subsequently re-exported to Pakistan and the Middle East.

Pashmina exports increased 16.85 percent to Rs3.76 billion, while footwear exports jumped 56.19 percent to Rs3.19 billion. Fabric exports rose 16.97 percent to Rs3.6 billion.

Dog chew exports increased 6.62 percent to Rs4.81 billion. Traders said major US brands have continued sourcing dog chews from Nepal despite a 10 percent US tariff and concerns over supply chain disruptions.

The National Strategic Work Plan (2026-2031) for dog chew exports aims to increase production and quality, diversify markets and introduce international food-safety certifications such as Hazard Analysis Critical Control Point and Good Manufacturing Practice.

Lentil exports rose 11.02 percent to Rs401 million, while ginger exports surged 157.38 percent to Rs1.5 billion. The government’s strategic work plan for ginger aims to increase productivity and value addition, develop processing facilities and diversify export markets.

Pasta exports increased 68.49 percent to Rs4 billion. Coffee exports rose 26.74 percent to Rs144.95 million, with 70 tonnes shipped, while honey exports increased 84.36 percent to Rs105.92 million.

Nepal first adopted the NTIS in 2010, identifying 12 goods and seven services for special support as part of efforts to make trade more inclusive and contribute to poverty reduction. The strategy was revised in 2016, reducing the list of priority goods and services to 12. Products including carpets, tea, felt and large cardamom were retained as priority export products.

articles.title: How Nepal manages unidentified and unclaimed bodies
articles.summary:
When an unidentified body is found in Nepal, police begin an investigation to establish the person’s identity and trace relatives before the remains are transferred to a hospital mortuary.

But with 788 unidentified and unclaimed bodies currently being kept in hospital facilities nationwide, limited storage capacity is forcing hospitals to begin disposal procedures within months.

The process starts at the local level. Police notify the relevant local government and ward representatives after an unidentified body is found. Under the Unidentified and Unclaimed Body Management Guidelines, 2021, police prepare an official inquest report in the presence of local representatives and residents.

If relatives are identified during the initial investigation, the body is handed over to them. If no relatives are found, the remains are transferred to a hospital mortuary for preservation while police continue efforts to establish the person’s identity.

According to Nepal Police data, 1,634 unidentified bodies have been recovered nationwide since fiscal year 2013-14. Of these, 133 were identified and handed over to their families, 84 were transferred to teaching hospitals for medical research, and 629 were cremated or buried after the required legal procedures. Another 788 remain in hospital mortuaries, awaiting identification or final disposal.

Deputy Inspector General of police Abi Narayan Kafle, central spokesperson of the police, said detailed records are maintained for every unidentified body.

“The police are always the first to arrive at the scene and complete all preliminary legal procedures,” Kafle said. “We maintain complete records of the deceased. If families looking for missing relatives examine these records carefully, identification becomes significantly easier.”

Police also publish photographs and details of unidentified bodies on their public online portal to help families looking for missing relatives.

But the system faces a major constraint: hospitals do not have enough space to preserve unidentified remains for extended periods.

International standards call for unidentified bodies to be preserved for up to 12 years to give families adequate time to trace missing relatives. Hospitals in Nepal, however, lack the infrastructure and storage capacity required for such long-term preservation.

Tribhuvan University Teaching Hospital in Kathmandu currently has 80 unidentified bodies in its mortuary and receives around 50 such bodies each year. Its mortuary has a maximum capacity of 150 bodies.

Gopal Kumar Chaudhary, head of the Forensic Department at TU Teaching Hospital, said the hospital contacts police three months after a body arrives to check whether relatives have been traced.

“We inquire with the police after three months to check whether any relatives have been traced,” Chaudhary said. “By the six-month mark, management procedures must begin to free up space for incoming bodies. Remains can realistically be preserved for six months at most.”

Patan Hospital in Lalitpur currently holds 16 unidentified bodies and has a mortuary capacity of 24. It keeps remains for up to a year before final disposal.

Some unidentified bodies are also allocated to medical education institutions for teaching purposes. Around 30 such bodies are provided to teaching institutions nationwide each year.

Srijana Kunwar, head of the Forensic Department at Patan Academy of Health Sciences, said PAHS receives only one body a year for academic instruction after approval from a specialised committee. The remains are given final rites after their academic use is completed.

For bodies transferred to medical institutions, the respective teaching hospitals are responsible for arranging final rites once academic use is completed and for maintaining records of the process.

The system therefore relies on police records and public disclosure to identify the deceased, while hospitals provide temporary storage. But the shortage of mortuary space means the period available to identify an unknown person and reunite the remains with their family is often far shorter than international preservation standards envisage.

articles.title: How Youssef Wehbe and Soma Fight Club are pushing Rabindra Dhant and Yuki Angdembe to the pinnacle of MMA
articles.summary:
It is not easy to get to train at Soma Fight Club in Bali, Indonesia. Youssef Wehbe, head MMA coach at the facility, is very picky about the fighters he lets in and be part of the family.

It is specifically the reason why Rabindra Dhant and Yuki Angdembe, two of Nepal’s elite MMA fighters, often mention Soma and its key role in shaping them before and after their fights.

When Angdembe and Dhant first entered Soma, they were treated with the respect that a fight gym abides by: show them hell on the first day.

“Yuki had sought a different gym in Bali,” Wehbe told the Post over a phone call recently. “He [Yuki] had come to Soma and said, ‘I wanna try this place’. Soma had just opened then. I said to myself, ‘If you wanna try me, MF, I am gonna smash you. I whipped his ass.”

Soma is about to complete its fifth year. And it has already become one of the go-to places for MMA training for fighters across the world. The facility has also earned a special place among Nepali combat sports fans.

“Now, I can’t get rid of him [Yuki],” said Wehbe, adding that the scenario was similar when Dhant first came to Soma with his coach Diwiz Piya a couple of years ago.

Wehbe hails from Lebanon. He went by the moniker ‘The Silverback’ during his fighting days. It was when he was training at Bali MMA, a premier martial arts and fitness academy in Indonesia, that he met Gianni Subba and Mike Ikilei—Wehbe’s teammate and striking coach, respectively. Subba and Mike then later opened Soma and called in Wehbe.

Subba was born to a Nepali father and a Malaysian mother. He was raised in Hawaii and Malaysia, and went on to become Malaysia’s foremost flyweight martial artist. It was Subba who first mentioned Dhant to Wehbe.

“Rabi was then fighting at ONE when Gianni told me about him,” Wehbe recalls. “Yuki also proudly mentioned Rabi.”

For Wehbe and Mike, when Dhant first reached Soma—with his coach Piya—he was an average fighter.

“Mike used to say he [Rabindra] is good. Okay. Average,” Wehbe said.

However, the more he learnt about Dhant and the more Dhant proved himself in the ring and training, the crazier Wehbe got.

“I measure individuals with others,” said Wehbe. “There is a guy—I won’t say the name—who beat Rabi to a pulp in the initial days. Now, Rabi goes toe to toe with him.”

Dhant’s story, as it is well known, is a motivating one—from a construction labourer to Nepal’s top MMA fighter. “It is a crazy story,” an elated Wehbe told the Post.

“Rabi was supposed to be a construction worker in Qatar. Now, see where his life choices took him. I always say it to Rabi: You are not supposed to be here. Take advantage.”

Since his pro MMA debut in 2019, Dhant has fought 11 bouts. And he has lost only one—which came against Pakistan’s Ismail Khan at ONE Championship on December 15, 2023.

It was especially when Dhant debuted at ONE and won his first fight—against Russia’s Torepchi Dongak on September 15, 2023—that made him popular among Nepalis. His star rose further when he defeated Indian favourite and champion Chungreng Koren and took the bantamweight title at Matrix Fight Night-17 in August last year.

“It was a big win for Rabi,” said Wehbe, who was in the ring side when Dhant defeated Koren in Uttar Pradesh, India. “Around six weeks before that fight, Dhant had torn his hamstring. He did not just recover after following specialised training plans at Soma… It was his mentality and Gorkha blood.”

Now, Dhant is on a path where no Nepali had ever wandered before—at the Road to UFC (RTU). Launched by the UFC in 2022, RTU is an annual, single-elimination tournament series that offers top rising prospects from the Asia-Pacific region a direct path to an official UFC contract.

There are three stages in Dhant’s bantamweight division at RTU Season 5—quarterfinal, semifinal and final. He has already won his first fight—against Kimbert Alintozon of the Philippines—in Macau in May.

“I was 100 percent sure that Rabi would win his fight against Kimbert,” said Wehbe. “We, including Mike, put plans for a year and more. And the way we all had prepared and trained, the win was visible from the very start.”

However, Wehbe says he cannot give a similar guarantee in Dhant’s upcoming fight at the semifinal, where Dhant is facing New Zealand’s Kasib Murdoch in Shanghai, China, on August 28.

“This will be Rabi’s greatest challenge to date,” Wehbe said. “Irrespective of the result for now, I am certain that it will be a very good fight.”

Nonetheless, Wehbe stressed that the “Soma family” is backing Dhant to the very end and working together to make sure he wins his next fight and then the final as well and earn a UFC contract.

“There are many MMA promotions in the world. Too many,” Wehbe said. “But the UFC is the pinnacle. Getting to fight at the UFC is a very big thing. And I want to see Rabi there.”

Soma is a family

Two days ago, Wehbe posted a group photo of the available fighters in Soma. Including Wehbe, there were individuals from 13 countries—Nepal, Lebanon, Ukraine, India, New Zealand, Australia, United States, Russia, Egypt, Armenia, Algeria and Turkey.

“That’s the beauty of Soma. We live and push each other like a family,” said Wehbe. “But it is not easy to be part of this family.”

Why does Soma place so much emphasis on the notion of “living like a family”?

“Family gives you extra power,” Wehbe said. “It is why we live like a family at Soma.”

Wehbe, Mike and Subba are the three main pillars that run Soma. They all hail from three different regions, thousands of miles apart.

“But what unites us is a deep love for our families. We—myself, Mike and Gianni—are deeply family-oriented people, and everything we do is to support them,” Wehbe said. “In a sport as dangerous as MMA, it’s your family who ultimately suffers through your sacrifices and celebrates your achievements.”

How much Wehbe loves his family, especially his daughter Ayouni, can be seen on his Instagram posts and stories.

And Wehbe says he sees a similar fire in Dhant. “Rabi isn’t just fighting for himself,” Wehbe continues, “but for everyone around him and everyone standing behind him.”

Angdembe has been in Soma for a long time. Dhant and Piya have been associated with that family for around two years now.

“No matter how long you’ve spent with Soma, once a part of the family, always a part,” said Wehbe. “Even Sisan [Baniya] is a part of Soma. He is a great guy too.”

Wehbe also expects that Bali has been a home-away-from-home for Dhant in another way as well: the gods.

“Rabi often visits temples of Hanuman and Shiva as Bali has a strong Hindu religion,” Wehbe said. “It is important because in combat sports, you do need a bit of luck that comes through blessing. I also feel Rabi gets stronger after he visits these temples in Bali.”

Fond of Nepalis

Wehbe spent his quality days—when he was a fighter—in the Gulf. When he lived in Dubai and Qatar, Wehbe often came across Nepalis.

“Many Nepalis do not have ideal jobs in Dubai and Qatar. But one needs to do it for money,” Wehbe said. “But Nepalis have a deep identity and great history from what I have learnt.”

Wehbe got to know Nepal closely through Subba. Then, there was Angdembe. And then Dhant and Piya.

“Right now, I have Nepali hats [dhaka topi] and Nepali knives [khukuri] of different sizes,” said Wehbe, who wore a dhaka topi when he entered the ring and celebrated Dhant’s win over Koren at MFN-17.

Wehbe insists on being present for every bout his fighters take, convinced that trust in the corner is paramount. Yet cornering Dhant and Angdembe revealed an unexpected highlight—the vocal loyalty of the Nepali diaspora.

“At MFN, the support Dhant and Angdembe had from Nepali fans so far from home was astonishing. It was in India, near to Nepal, so it was believable,” Wehbe recalled. “But to see even a bigger crowd in Macau, I was damned.”

Wehbe says he was not the only one to be surprised at Dhant’s supporters in Macau.

“It was not just me. Even the UFC was shocked to see such a big crowd, and that too not for the main cards,” Wehbe remembers. “Once Rabi’s fight was over, the venue was almost empty. I also saw videos of Nepalis gathering in different places back home to watch Rabi’s fight. I have to admit it, Nepali fans are extremely supportive of their athletes. I hope to see a similar crowd in Shanghai too.”

There is one more thing Wehbe loved about Nepali supporters: the way they accept and love back people who love them.

“Zack had asked Yuki for Nepal’s flag before entering the ring at MFN-17. And when Nepali fans saw it, they accepted Zack as their own in no time,” Wehbe recalls. “At the end of the fight, after Zack won, he even screamed ‘Jay Nepal’. The next thing, Zack got a nickname from Nepali fans. He is now Zack “Bahadur” Bennet.”

Bennet hails from New Zealand and was fighting Afghanistan’s Abdul Fazeel before the Dhant vs Koren main event at MFN-17. Bennet won by split decision. He now holds a professional record of 6-0.

“The whole of Soma is in love with Nepali culture. Everyone supports and loves Rabi, Diwiz and Yuki,” Wehbe told the Post. “And this trio love and support them back wholeheartedly.”

“Nepal, invest in MMA”

Wehbe has understood how much Nepalis love this combat sport. And he wants to see Nepal reach great heights in MMA.

“Firstly, the fighters your country has. Rabi and Yuki are already at a high level; not the highest though. There are many more youngsters coming up, such as Rahul [Hamal Thakuri] and Kunjan [Kakshapati], among others,” says Wehbe. “But they need more and better facilities and resources to challenge the world.”

So, what does Wehbe suggest for Nepal?

“Just give some money to Diwiz, and he will take Nepali MMA to the next level,” Wehbe said on a serious note. “You also need a federation for MMA and get affiliated with the International Mixed Martial Arts Federation (IMMAF). And that should be led by Diwiz.”

There is a specific reason why Wehbe has so much trust in Piya.

“Diwiz is a very good guy. It is not easy to let your fighter be coached by someone else. Diwiz brought Rabi to Soma because he wanted Rabi to get better. These two—Diwiz and Rabi—complete each other. There is no Diwiz without Rabi, and no Rabi without Diwiz.”

He also has high praise for Angdembe.

“Yuki started MMA far sooner than Rabi. There are not many fighters who would want others to get ahead of them. But it was Yuki who told me about Rabi and asked to have him in,” Wehbe said. “Even now, Yuki supports Rabi every time, in every way possible. He does not care if Rabi is getting ahead of them. But I am sure Yuki will also soon get a chance at RTU because he is a good fighter who gives his all.”

Wehbe also has a huge respect for Nepal’s history.

“You all come from a country that was never colonised,” Wehbe said. “There are a handful of countries like Nepal. And the Gorkhali mentality, wow. You must channel this mentality into MMA.”

Wehbe also wants Nepalis to take a lesson from Dhant’s journey.

“I do not want to say that every Nepali should take up MMA,” Wehbe added. “What Nepalis and many others can learn from Rabi is that you just need to chase your dreams and take risks in anything you do.”

After over half an hour of phone conversation and a final question of what he wants from Dhant, Angdembe and overall Nepali MMA, Wehbe responded, “To see these fighters and Nepali MMA improve, improve, improve and improve.”

articles.title: How Nepali diaspora literature confronts borders and belonging
articles.summary:
The invitation I received early this month from the Centre for Nepal Studies UK to participate in a live webinar on the topic ‘How does diaspora writing reshape the Nepali literary sphere?’ impressed me in several ways. Nepali diaspora writing has strongly drawn the attention of researchers, Nepali writers and literary critics over the years. Literary writers and critics have been eloquent on this subject. The participants were Nepali fiction writer Neelam Karki Niharika, travel writer Krishna Bajgai and my former student and well-known scholar Mahesh Paudyal. Sangita Swechcha curated the webinar.

Diasporic writing has become a popular subject among writers within and outside Nepal, even though it may require further discussion and writing to conclude that it has transformed Nepali writing. Discussions of the Nepali diaspora encompass both broad and minuscule issues. Debates about the role of the Nepali diaspora, especially in Darjeeling, Sikkim, Assam and other places, have undergone various metamorphoses throughout history. Nepalis and their role in contributing to the formation of states and territorial administrations in India have gone down in history.

The first phase of diaspora is one of ambivalence. Literary writers of the early generations, all based and active in Darjeeling, expressed ambivalence in their writing and in their shifting bases between India and Nepal. The pioneers known by the acronym Su Dha Pa or Surya Bikram Gyawali, Dharanidhar Sharma and Paras Mani Pradhan represent that diasporic ambivalence in Nepali writing and activism. Surya Bikram Gyawali became the writer of ‘brave Nepali history’ (in the words of historian Pratyoush Onta) and the Chancellor of the Royal Nepal Academy. Dharanidhar moved to Nepal.

Literature has played a quiet role. Obtrusive and unobtrusive modes can be identified in this regard. Lain Singh Bangdel’s position was similar to Gyawali’s. Bangdel also became Chancellor of the Royal Nepal Academy, but his famous diasporic novel Muluk Bahira, or ‘outside the native land ’, pulsates with ambivalence and a quest for diasporic identity. Lil Bahadur Chetri’s Basain has become a classic of migration literature, as the title suggests. Many examples exist.

The fuzzy border of diaspora should be noted here. Literature production in Banaras became possible through ‘print capitalism’, to use Francesca Orseni’s expression, in the second half of the 19th century and continued well into the early decades of the 20th century. This deserves discussion in relation to diasporic literature. Production, readership and sales were the words of print capitalism. The printing of Bhanubhakta Acharya’s Ramayana brings together these various strands of the early diasporic anxieties. The mantra of the early Indic Nepali diaspora was the quest, and its primary means was producing texts. Banaras’ print capitalism saw the publication of many books and literary magazines. Then came the literary textbook production of Paras Mani Pradhan. The carefully prepared diasporic texts were our textbooks. I grew up with them without ever thinking about who had created and produced them.

So what I call the productive ambivalence of books from the first phase of the Indic Nepali diaspora was part of the educational campaign. We should look at this with a broader perspective. The fuzzy lines between native and diasporic literature remained a force of a certain order for a long time. They persisted well into the writings of Indra Rai and the Tesro Ayam. The diasporic line became broader. Later, the idioms changed. Literary writers became Indian Nepali writers. The motif of the ‘muluk bahira’ psyche was not strongly evoked even in earlier times. Govinda Bhattarai’s novel Muglan is an important intervention in that area. Written by a Nepali writer with diasporic sympathy and empathy, this novel evokes Muglan’s conditionality. I would call it an important meta-fictional work on the theme of diasporic imaginaire.

Ramji Timilsina, a fine scholar and my erstwhile student and a PhD on diasporic literature, in an article titled ‘Use and Misuse of ‘Diaspora’ in Nepali Literary Discourse’ says, “Those who have crossed the border of Nepal, have permanently settled in a new nation, and have grown a community that resembles and reflects Nepal are the members of the Nepali Diaspora.” He further adds, “They maintain and grow contacts and relations with the homeland through its members and make physical visits to it; they make use of communication”. Timilsina concludes, “These features show that a diaspora is different from transnational mobile communities and the transnational outsiders.”

Literary critics and historians assert that the geographical and national spaces of the Nepali Diaspora are in India, Bhutan and Burma. The other category of the incipient Nepali Diaspora, as commonly discussed, is England, USA, Canada and Australia. Nepali diaspora is growing. But we must address the earlier category again. I have heard in interactions and read in writings that the ambivalence of the Nepali diaspora in the case of the Nepalis in India is evoked frequently. We ask: Are the established Indian Nepali writers diasporic? I think they are Indian Nepali writers. They do not maintain the nostalgia or angst related to the original land in the same way as writers of earlier times.

The question of readership in diasporic literature is important; it deserves serious discussion and engagement. This calls for expanding readership and working with a psyche of sharing. I think this is already happening and should be seen as an important shift in readership and in the creation of a readership sphere in different countries. The growing diasporic population, rising interest in writing, and the availability of sharing tools are notable. I think this phenomenon has become an important reality that will affect the very nature of diasporic literature and the praxis of sharing and spreading.

Another feature is the careful and subtle creation of the diasporic experience by native writers and publishing them either in the original language, such as Nepali and Nepal Bhasha, or getting them translated into English. I want to mention one such novel titled 17 September written in Nepal Bhasha by Malla K Sundar and translated into English by the Lisbon-based scholar Jyoti Tuladhar.

Nepali diasporic literary output is growing. The spheres of writing are expanding. With this, the identification of diasporic Nepali writings and writers is also growing. Connectivity and organisational networks have created a unique condition in diasporic literature. Literary organisations like the International Nepali Literary Society (Anesasa), along with visits by writers from Nepal to other countries, have fostered a culture of connectivity that encourages diasporic literature. Efforts are made to build cross-national readership by familiarising readers with works by diasporic writers. Launching their work in Nepal, especially in Kathmandu, organising interactions with them and creating literary awards are some productive activities.

articles.title: The state kept only one copy
articles.summary:
Every person who has waited in a malpot (Land Registration) office for a copy of lalpurja (Land Ownership Certificate) knows that moment. Someone walks into the back room and comes out with the sresta, a ledger too heavy to fit flat on the table. He dips his thumb in water, flips through pages and locates your record. Whatever is written, there is the truth about your land, as far as the state cares. Since those ledgers were burned in the Gen Z protests of September, all the land transactions in some districts just ceased, waiting for someone to recreate a ledger again, one owner at a time.

Last week, the Auditor General Toyam Raya told the Public Accounts Committee how much we lost. Records of 179 public bodies were destroyed during the protests of September 8-9. Around Rs148 billion worth of government transactions never got audited because of this. It can be recollected from the banks’ statements and government software, but the proof of whether it was done legally was burned down.

His deputy, Deepak Lamichhane, pointed out that the records could be reconstructed using the general vouchers that survived and internal audit reports. Reconstruction sounds like a lot, but lawmakers sitting in that room dismissed any notion that an office cannot be audited due to loss of papers.

My field is governed by a rule known as 3-2-1. Every piece of information you cannot afford to lose should have three copies, two kinds of storage, and one of them should be in another place altogether. It is not smart, and it is not novel, but this is exactly why every serious laboratory follows it without a thought. The rule assumes that the building will be destroyed, but does not bother speculating how.

Nepal followed this rule in one place, and it saved us. The Integrated Data Management Centre is located in Singha Durbar. While the fires ravaged other buildings around it, the centre came through unharmed, and its recovery site in Hetauda was never threatened. “The country would have gone blank,” said Manish Bhattarai, who runs that centre. He was not overstating. This building stores the information of Nepal Rastra Bank, the Home Ministry and police databases, company registry, Nagarik App and websites of all 753 local governments.

The same logic saved the land records. An estimate suggests that a million land documents burned in those two days, but people can still reclaim what belongs to them thanks to the existence of this information in the central system. Investment Board Nepal lost its own servers and hard disks in that fire, but it managed to preserve its files because they were stored at that centre and not in its own building.

The Supreme Court had no such arrangement. Basic details of the cases, such as party names and case numbers, were kept digitally, but the files themselves were paper-based. Roughly 20,000 pending case files and a far greater number of those with verdicts issued were burned. For several months, the court has been restoring this information by publishing notices urging litigants and their lawyers to come with photocopies of their files. Over 17,000 were restored by July. The real backup, it turns out, was hiding in photocopy shops outside the courthouse gates.

This is the thing that worries me. In the budget, a sovereign AI compute centre was announced, tentatively in Syuchatar, and the purchase of thousands of processors to operate it. I was arguing for it, and I still do. But no model is as good as the records it relies upon. Two days before this announcement, The Kathmandu Post reported that government servers were malfunctioning all over the country and that a single software breakdown took land revenue offices offline in all 77 districts. Most government data centres’ servers are seven or eight years old and have already reached the point where nobody can support them anymore. We plan to compute on the data we have no idea how to save.

During the same hearing, Finance Minister Swarnim Wagle promised the government will digitise government records and follow any instruction issued by the committee. Nobody offered a deadline. Nobody asked who will audit it. There is still no rule requiring every ordinary district office, ward office or school to store a copy of its records in another place.

The usual objection to this idea is the cost. Half of it is legitimate. Digitising millions of pages is a very slow and expensive process, as the Supreme Court discovered for itself this year. Holding a second copy of information already digitised is not. Storing it costs a bit more now than it used to, because of the current worldwide rush into AI which pushed memory prices sharply up. It is nothing compared to the cost of importing processors.

Underneath all of this lurks the question of what people get away with. Once the records of 179 public bodies disappear, the proof of any questionable information they contained disappears with them. I am not suggesting that someone set the building on fire to hide a ledger. I am saying that we created a state in which such an excuse becomes permanently available.

There will be speeches about rebuilding next month. It is easy to buy some furniture. Nobody said anything about the srestha in the backroom, and until someone does it, the next fire will cost us the same as this one.

articles.title: Banning crypto isn’t working. It’s time to regulate it
articles.summary:
Crypto-assets, which include cryptocurrencies, stablecoins, non-fungible tokens (NFTs), and tokenised deposits, have evolved from a niche experiment into a platform for digital transformation. With the market maturing, the underlying technology better understood, and clarity in regulations, they are redesigning the future payment system, moving value as seamlessly as data. Due to its unique characteristics of decentralised infrastructure, borderless transactions, and privacy concerns, conventional regulatory frameworks cannot effectively govern this technology.

Nepal’s approach toward digital assets is restrictive. Digital assets are not permitted in Nepal. This cautious approach by the Nepal Rastra Bank is understandable for a country with capital controls, shallow financial market infrastructure and heavy dependence on remittance inflows.

With Nepal receiving around $10 billion in annual remittances, and an increasing number of Nepalis participating in the global gig economy, the need for a comprehensive digital assets policy has become pressing. If blockchain and the crypto industry can be regulated and managed, it can unlock new economic opportunities critical for a growing economy.

Globally, the suitability of the approach depends upon market maturity, regulatory readiness, consumer awareness, perceived threat to financial stability, potential opportunities and other local nuances.
